title: How avoided emissions can help unlock investment in low-carbon innovation
gist: The GHG Protocol's Scope 1/2/3 architecture penalizes manufacturers whose products cut customers' emissions, and a parallel 'avoided emissions' metric is now being institutionalized via WBCSD guidance (2023-2026), an IEC International Standard published early 2026, and a GHG Protocol public consultation. Japanese industrials (Toray, Daikin, Panasonic) and investors (Nomura Asset Management, Schroders) are the early adopters, with Toray targeting a 25-fold increase in avoided emissions by 2030 and Panasonic 200Mt+ annually by 2050.

insights.claim: The GHG Protocol's Scope 1/2/3 architecture is described as being at an inflection point after more than two decades, under pressure from regulators, investors and decision-makers to produce metrics that guide real-world capital allocation rather than only measure emissions accurately.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
insights.so_what: Reporting-standard change is a slow-moving but repricing-relevant variable: firms currently scored badly on absolute emissions may be re-rated if a second, opportunity-side metric gains official status.
insights.quote: the global emissions reporting architecture is at an inflection point
insights.locator: After more than two decades in place

insights.claim: Current carbon accounting structurally disadvantages upstream materials and equipment makers whose products reduce end-user emissions, because there is no institutional framework crediting that reduction against the producer's own footprint.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
insights.so_what: Screens that rank companies purely on reported Scope 1-3 systematically under-weight enabling-technology suppliers; that mispricing is the trade the avoided-emissions push is trying to close.
insights.quote: no institutional framework or standard recognizes that 7% as a legitimate contribution to the reduction of the company’s overall carbon footprint
insights.locator: Gaps in current carbon accounting standards

insights.claim: The perverse outcome flagged is that a company growing sales of low-emitting products shows rising reported emissions, since use-phase emissions of sold products scale with volume even as society-wide emissions fall.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
insights.so_what: Emissions-intensity trajectories are an unreliable short signal for climate-solution scalers; expect divergence between reported footprint growth and genuine transition contribution.
insights.quote: The firm was concerned that an investee’s emissions were shown as increasing, despite contributions to reduce society-wide emissions through increased sales of low-emitting products.
insights.locator: As a leading financial services group, Nomura

insights.claim: Toray's carbon fibre reinforced plastics let a Boeing aircraft weigh up to 20% less than a conventional model, translating to roughly a 7% lifecycle emissions reduction for that aircraft.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
insights.so_what: A quantified enablement ratio for advanced materials in aerospace — the kind of number that becomes a valuation input if avoided emissions get standardized.

insights.claim: Daikin's 2024 footprint was 313.09 million tons of CO2, of which 262.6 million tons (83.9%) came from customer use of its products, while more efficient product sales cut 48.2 million tons of CO2 in that same use phase.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
insights.so_what: For HVAC and appliance names, ~84% of the footprint sits in use phase, so efficiency gains are the only material lever — and a metric change could flip the narrative on an apparent high emitter.

insights.claim: Panasonic already measures and discloses a proprietary 'Contribution Impact' metric for how its products reduce users' GHG emissions and is publicly lobbying for an internationally recognized standard to measure and report it.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
insights.so_what: Corporate lobbying for a new accounting standard is a tell on where incumbents think their disclosure advantage lies; first movers on the metric will look best when it is codified.

insights.claim: Toray targets a 25-fold increase in avoided emissions by 2030 relative to its 2013 baseline, and Panasonic targets 200 million tons or more of avoided emissions annually by 2050.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
insights.so_what: These are explicit, datable corporate KPIs to track; a 25x target implies aggressive volume growth in enabling materials, not just efficiency improvement.
insights.locator: In response to this growing investor interest

insights.claim: WBCSD defines avoided emissions as the positive impact from comparing a low-carbon solution's GHG impact against a counterfactual scenario without that solution, making the metric inherently baseline-dependent rather than directly measured.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
insights.so_what: Counterfactual-based metrics are gameable; diligence should focus on the chosen baseline and reference scenario, not the headline tonnage.
insights.quote: positive impact created when comparing the GHG impact of a low-carbon solution to an alternative scenario without that solution in place

insights.claim: The key methodological guardrail is that avoided emissions must be calculated and reported separately and distinctly from a company's GHG inventory, never netted against it — the earlier practice of deducting them is cited as what discredited the concept.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
insights.so_what: A red flag for screening disclosures: any issuer subtracting avoided emissions from its inventory is using a discredited presentation and invites restatement risk.
insights.quote: corporate disclosures which deducted avoided emissions from the reporting entities’ regular GHG inventory were confusing to readers

insights.claim: The GX League frames avoided emissions as a way to shift climate disclosure from risk-only framing toward climate-related opportunities of the reporting entity.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
insights.so_what: A disclosure regime that surfaces upside creates a channel for climate-tech revenue narratives to enter mainstream financial reporting rather than sitting in sustainability appendices.
insights.locator: They emphasized the importance of avoided emissions

insights.claim: The concept is not new: the chemical industry published an avoided-emissions assessment methodology in 2013, and TCFD's 2017 final report already included 'avoided GHG emissions through the entire product life cycle' in its recommended metrics-and-targets disclosure.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
insights.so_what: A 13-year gestation suggests the current push is a late-stage institutionalization rather than a novel idea — the bottleneck has been adoption, not invention.
insights.locator: For certain industries, the concept is nothing new

insights.claim: The IEC published an International Standard early in 2026 on quantifying and communicating avoided emissions from relevant products and systems, giving electrical and electronic manufacturers a formal reference for the first time.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
insights.so_what: A live standard means audit-grade numbers are now possible for electronics and equipment names — the practical precondition for investors to underwrite the metric.
insights.locator: Early in 2026, the International Electrotechnical Commission

insights.claim: Later in 2026 the GHG Protocol itself opened a public consultation on an 'actions and market instruments' white paper containing a section on avoided emissions from use of sold products, which the authors read as the decisive signal of mainstreaming.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
insights.so_what: Watch this consultation's outcome — the governing body of GHG inventory engaging is the single highest-leverage catalyst for the metric becoming investable.
insights.locator: Later in the year, the GHG Protocol initiated a public consultation

insights.claim: Political cover arrived quickly after WBCSD's March 2023 report, with G7 energy and environment ministers meeting in Sapporo acknowledging avoided emissions in their ministerial communique.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
insights.so_what: G7-level endorsement plus Japanese industrial sponsorship means the metric has state backing, lowering the odds it fades as a voluntary experiment.
insights.locator: Soon after the launch of WBCSD’s first report

insights.claim: The authors argue the binding constraint is no longer methodology but financial-sector adoption, since development so far has been driven by high-emitting industries with an interest in the outcome.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
insights.so_what: An implicit admission of conflict of interest — until independent allocators price the metric, avoided-emissions disclosures should be treated as issuer-favourable marketing.
insights.quote: The development of evaluation methodologies on avoided emissions has so far largely been driven by high-emitting industries. What is needed now is buy-in from investors and financial actors.
insights.locator: A pivotal role for finance on avoided emissions

insights.claim: Nomura Asset Management adopted avoided emissions as a growth-potential metric after finding that climate analysis of its equity portfolio using corporate GHG emissions alone was limiting, and Nomura published a report on whether the metric enhances enterprise value from an investor's perspective.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
insights.so_what: Reframing avoided emissions as a growth proxy rather than an ESG score is the mechanism by which it enters fundamental valuation models.
insights.locator: In the climate-related analysis of its equity portfolio

insights.claim: London-based Schroders uses avoided emissions specifically as a proxy for an investee's ability to attract future market demand, not as an ethical screen.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
insights.so_what: This reframes a sustainability metric as a demand-forecasting input — a use case that survives ESG backlash because it is revenue-driven, not values-driven.
insights.quote: Schroders sees it as a means to evaluate its investees’ potential ability to attract demand from the market.

insights.claim: Embedding avoided emissions in investment and lending decisions is presented as the incentive mechanism that would push technology-holding corporates to scale low-carbon solutions faster.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
insights.so_what: Watch for the metric appearing in sustainability-linked loan KPIs and transition-finance taxonomies; that would be the point cost of capital actually moves.
insights.locator: Incorporating avoided emissions in investment and lending

insights.claim: The authors concede the process is early and that baselines, reference scenarios and attribution remain unresolved technical elements requiring refined definitions plus disclosure of calculation conditions.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
insights.so_what: Attribution across a value chain is the crux: without it, the same avoided ton can be claimed by the material supplier, the OEM and the operator, inflating aggregate claims.
insights.quote: We can start by setting more refined definitions for technical elements such as baselines, reference scenarios and attributions, while encouraging the disclosure of calculation conditions.
